bottom_line: In chronic heart failure, high-dose vs low-dose lisinopril did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.92 [0.82–1.03]).
implications: These data support that, versus low-dose lisinopril, high-dose lisinopril produced a statistically significant reduction in the combined endpoint of all-cause mortality plus hospitalization for any reason (hazard ratio 0.88 [0.82–0.96]) but did not show a statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality alone (hazard ratio 0.92 [0.82–1.03], P=0.128).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind comparison of low-dose vs high-dose lisinopril strategies.
major_points.quote: Those who could tolerate 12.5 to 15 mg daily for $2 weeks were randomly assigned (double-blind, 1:1 ratio) to either a low-dose or high-dose ACE inhibitor strategy.

major_points.text: Population: NYHA class II–IV heart failure with ejection fraction ≤30%.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 3164 patients with New York Heart Association class II to IV heart failure and an ejection fraction #30%

major_points.text: Dose targets: 2.5–5.0 mg daily (low-dose) vs 32.5–35 mg daily (high-dose).
major_points.quote: The target dose of lisinopril was 2.5 to 5.0 mg daily in the low-dose group and 32.5 to 35 mg daily in the high-dose group.

major_points.text: Primary end point was all-cause mortality; result was not statistically significant.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was all-cause mortality

major_points.text: All-cause mortality: 717 (44.9) vs 666 (42.5), hazard ratio 0.92 (0.82–1.03), P=0.128.
High-dose reduced the combined risk of all-cause mortality plus hospitalization for any reason: hazard ratio 0.88 (0.82–0.96), P=0.002.

absolute_effects.text: All-cause mortality plus hospitalization for any reason: 1338 (83.8) vs 1250 (79.7).
Hospitalizations for heart failure (total number): 1576 vs 1199.
Worsening heart failure adverse experience: 709 (44) vs 594 (38).

subgroups.text: Reduction in risk for death or hospitalization for any reason was similar regardless of age, sex, cause of heart failure, ejection fraction, or NYHA class.
subgroups.quote: The reduction in risk was similar regardless of age, sex, cause of heart failure, ejection fraction, or NYHA class (Figure 2).

subgroups.text: Effect on mortality in subgroups was not different from the overall effect.
subgroups.quote: The effect on mortality in subgroups was not different from the overall effect (Figure 2).

harms.text: Dizziness adverse experience was more frequent with high-dose (19% vs 12%).
Worsening renal function adverse experience was more frequent with high-dose (10% vs 7%).
Hyperkalemia adverse experience was more frequent with high-dose (6% vs 4%).
Open-label tolerability phase: 176 withdrawn for possible side effects as dose increased toward 12.5 to 15 mg.
harms.quote: 176 patients were withdrawn for possible side effects when the dose of lisinopril was increased toward 12.5 to 15 mg

guidelines_referenced.quote: Task Force of the Working Group on Heart Failure of the European Society of Cardiology. The treatment of heart failure.

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class II, III, or IV symptoms of heart failure associated with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤30%.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were recruited into the ATLAS study if they had New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV symptoms of heart failure associated with a left ventricular ejection fraction #30%

inclusion_criteria.text: Class II symptoms required prior emergency room or hospital treatment for heart failure within 6 months.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients with class II symptoms were required to have received treatment for heart failure in an emergency room or hospital within 6 months.

inclusion_criteria.text: Able to tolerate 12.5 to 15 mg daily of open-label lisinopril for at least 2 weeks.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Those who could tolerate 12.5 to 15 mg daily for $2 weeks were randomly assigned

exclusion_criteria.text: Acute coronary ischemic event or revascularization procedure within 2 months.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded if they had had an acute coronary ischemic event or revascularization procedure within 2 months

analysis_methods.text: Planned 90% power to detect a 15% relative difference in mortality (two-tailed alpha 0.05).
analysis_methods.quote: would have 90% power to detect a 15% relative difference in mortality between the treatment groups (a50.05, 2-tailed).

analysis_methods.text: Primary endpoint significance threshold at scheduled end was P<0.0394 due to interim analyses.
analysis_methods.quote: comparisons of the 2 treatments for all-cause mortality at the scheduled end of the trial were considered significant if P,0.0394 was attained

analysis_methods.text: Kaplan-Meier time-to-first-event plots and log-rank test used.
analysis_methods.quote: Cumulative survival curves were constructed as time-to-first- event plots by Kaplan-Meier survivorship methods, and differences between the curves were tested for significance by both the log-rank statistic

analysis_methods.text: Cox proportional hazard regression model adjusted for NYHA class and ejection fraction.
analysis_methods.quote: a Cox proportional hazard regression model, adjusted (as protocol-specified) for NYHA class and ejection fraction.

analysis_methods.text: Analyses included all randomized patients and used the intention-to-treat principle.
analysis_methods.quote: The analyses included all randomized patients, and all events were assigned to the patient’s randomized treatment group (according to the intention-to-treat principle).

criticisms.text: The primary endpoint (death) was not significantly different between treatment groups.
criticisms.quote: Nevertheless, the present study did not observe a signifi- cant difference between the 2 treatment groups in the risk of death, the primary end point of the study.

criticisms.text: The trial cannot predict effects versus placebo or versus intermediate doses.
criticisms.quote: our results cannot predict what we might have observed if low doses of ACE inhibitors had been compared with placebo or if high doses of ACE inhibitors had been compared with intermediate doses of these drugs.

criticisms.text: Sample size assumptions may have been affected by a lower-than-expected mortality rate and by patients not being maintained on assigned medications.
criticisms.quote: Yet the observed annual mortality rate in the trial was only 15%, and many patients were not maintained on their assigned study medications.
